lines: d41: 📖 The Codex turns a page on its own. Brooklyn Nikolaev is dead. You didn't ask. It knew.
d41: Nobody's talking much. The fire feels smaller tonight.
d41: 🕯️ Brooklyn Nikolaev is dead — the expedition. The village stops. Somebody screams. Somebody else starts digging.
d41: What Brooklyn kept close goes into the ground with them — keepsakes are buried, never taken from the body.
d41: "Brooklyn's gone." Aurora looks at you for a long moment. "You're not Brooklyn." No heat in it. Just fact. You'll have to earn this face.
d41: The Codex doesn't pause for grief. Dwayne blinks — and it's already there, overlaying everything, syncing. No pen. No paper. The mantle just... transfers.
d41: 📖 LEARNED: Steady Hands (Level 1). Fine work under pressure. Dressing game, stitching wounds, tying snares — no shake.
d41: 📖 LEARNED: Old World Caches (Level 1). You know where people hid things: under floorboards, in hollow trees, behind loose bricks.
d41: 📖 LEARNED: Reading People (Level 1). Microexpressions leak truth. Watch the eyes, not the mouth. People tell you who they are.
d41: ⚡ TECHNIQUE UNLOCKED: Deep Read! You don't just read trust — you read intent. Know what they'll do next. (Your knowledge of Reading People amplifies your open_book.)
d41: 📖 LEARNED: Food Preservation (Level 1). Salt, smoke, dry. The big three. Salt draws water out; bacteria can't live without it.

d41: 📖 LEARNED: Diplomatic Incident (Level 1). Trust builds 2x faster. You're TOO good though — once per week you can start a diplomatic incident: villagers argue, you pick the winner (+trust with them, -trust with the loser).
d41: 🌟 "MANTLE TRANSFER DETECTED. ...Oh! New face! Same job! Whole new set of tricks. We hardly noticed. (That is a lie. We noticed. The audience CRIED.)"
d41: 📖 The Codex turns a page: Brooklyn Nikolaev, 41 days. The mantle passes to Dwayne Gupta.
d41: 🪞 You wake up somebody else. Dwayne Gupta, 73 — a pottery instructor. Their hands know different work now: Green Whisper.
d41: The village's quarrel was with Brooklyn — and Brooklyn is dead. The sentence doesn't cross the grave. You're someone else now; the docket is empty, but the village remembers.
d41: At the grave, Aurora, Roman, Marisol and 7 more speak for Dwayne — "Brooklyn trusted them. We saw it. Give them the fire's hearing." The village listens.
d41: The fire knew Dwayne before the Codex did — their name already carried weight here.
